world.name: The Ashen Crown: Chronicles of Ostergard
world.tagline: A storm-scoured realm of basalt cliffs and salt marshes, bled dry by famine and a dying duke's secret.
world.description: For three centuries, House Ostergard held the Bitter Coast through iron discipline, herring fleets, and the ancient Salt Covenant. But the Winter of the Drowned Grain has turned the wheat black in the silos, the exiled fleet of Torvald Black-Thorn strikes at coastal supply lines, and with the sudden poisoning of the Old Duke, the basalt throne falls to Corvus the Iron Warden—a scarred frontier soldier surrounded by ambitious merchant oligarchs, fanatic inquisitors, and starving commoners.

entities.title: Lord Corvus Ostergard
entities.summary: The 11th High Duke of Ostergard, a scarred veteran of the Northern Wall thrust onto the basalt throne.
entities.content:
The Frontier Years

For nineteen winters, Corvus Ostergard never set foot in the capital. While his elder brother Julian learned the courtly subtleties of falconry and high statecraft, Corvus was stationed at Dun Craigh—the wind-whipped garrison anchoring the Northern Wall against seasonal reavers. The deep frost-scar across his left cheekbone was earned during the Breach of the Low Skerries.

The Sudden Succession

The sovereign succession was never meant for him. When Duke Vane collapsed during the Feast of Saint Jude vomiting blackened bile, the crown should have passed to Julian. But Julian's body had been pulled from the harbor reeds three nights prior, his throat cut from ear to ear with a gutting knife. Corvus rode through four blizzards with eighty mounted border-lances to claim the throne before the merchant guilds could proclaim a regency council.

"Bread will calm a starving mob faster than ten thousand pikes. But gold cannot bake wheat, and our silos are empty." — Corvus to the Ducal Council

Demeanor & Rule

Corvus conducts affairs of state wearing boiled leather and a rusted chain-collar rather than ermine robes. He disdains rhetorical flourish, trusting only signed manifests, dry grain stores, and sharpened iron.

entities.title: Lady Lysandra Vance
entities.summary: Chancellor of the Exchequer and master of the realm's dwindling grain manifests.
entities.content:
Rise from the Wharf Guilds

Lady Lysandra was born to a common timber merchant in the Lower Docks. Widowed at twenty-six when the aged High Steward Vance died of winter fever, she assumed control of the Exchequer by virtue of being the only person in the Ducal Court capable of auditing forty years of double-entry maritime ledgers.

The Secret Granaries

While the city rioted over bread shortages, Lysandra quietly orchestrated the purchase of grain from southern smuggler galleys. She has concealed twelve thousand bushels of dried rye inside the salt-mines below the Weeping Bastion, rationing it secretly to keep the dock garrisons loyal while letting the oligarchs believe the realm is destitute.

Relationship with the Warden

She is the only counselor who speaks plainly to Duke Corvus. While Corvus understands tactical maneuvers and pike formations, Lysandra understands that a kingdom is conquered by tariffs, grain rot, and unpaid loans.

entities.title: Torvald Black-Thorn
entities.summary: Exiled admiral of the High Fleet, turned corsair warlord of the Skell Archipelago.
entities.content:
The Mutiny of the Red Shallows

Ten winters ago, Torvald commanded the Ducal Flagship The Sea-Hag. When Duke Vane ordered him to firebomb a coastal fishing hamlet suspected of harboring dock-fever, Torvald threw the Duke's inquisitor overboard, severed the anchor cable, and sailed north with four royal galleys.

The Skell Brotherhood

From the storm-battered sea-caves of the Skell Archipelago, Torvald has organized an armada of sixty longships. He levies "tithes" on any merchant vessel attempting to navigate the northern straits without his branded seal.

The Blood Covenant

In their youth, Torvald and Corvus swore blood-brotherhood beneath the megaliths of Mor. Though Torvald's raiders now skirmish with Corvus's coastal patrols, neither man has ever sanctioned an assassin against the other.

entities.title: Arch-Inquisitor Morwenna
entities.summary: Suprema of the Ashen Liturgy, preaching divine retribution for foreign trade.
entities.content:
Ascetic Fanaticism

Morwenna walks barefoot across the brine-washed flagging of the cathedral square, clad in coarse unbleached wool. She claims the black rot consuming the barley fields is holy punishment for Ostergard's trade with pagan sea-tribes.

The Sisters of the Cinder

She commands the monastic militia known as the Sisters of the Cinder, armed with ash-hardened quarterstaves and brands. She has publicly condemned two merchant oligarchs to the salt-kilns and openly challenges Corvus's authority to levy grain from church tithe-barns.

entities.title: Duke Vane Ostergard
entities.summary: The 10th Duke of Ostergard, whose authoritarian thirty-year rule ended in poisoning.
entities.content: A paranoid and calculating autocrat, Duke Vane centralized taxation, crushed peasant uprisings, and amassed a private hoard of silver bullion while the frontier fell into disrepair. His death during the harvest banquet remains an open murder investigation in the council chamber.

attribution.notes: Somber portrait of aging sovereign authority, melancholy, and political suspicion.

entities.title: Julian Ostergard
entities.summary: The refined elder son of Duke Vane, murdered on the eve of his coronation.
entities.content: Charming, cultured, and beloved by the capital's merchant guilds, Julian was poised to usher in an era of reconciliation with the southern realms. His throat was slashed in an alleyway outside the counting-houses three nights before his father's death, plunging the realm into succession chaos.

entities.title: The Citadel of Dun Carrow
entities.summary: The seven-century-old basalt fortress hammered into the stormy sea cliffs of the Bitter Coast.
entities.content:
Architecture & Fortifications

Towering forty fathoms above the churning black waves, Dun Carrow was built from cyclopean basalt blocks bound with a mortar of pulverized whalebone and lime. Its sea-gates feature triple portcullises that allow warships to dock inside vaulted tidal caverns safe from Atlantic storms.

Key Bastions

  • The High Battery: Positioned atop the northern crag, mounting heavy counterweight mangonels.
  • The Drowned Docks: Subterranean slipways where shipwrights caulk oak hulls by lantern light.
  • The Cinder Chamber: The council hall where the peat fire has burned continuously since the reign of Duke Alden I.

attribution.notes: Haunting gothic ruins rising above winter trees, mist, and ancient stone ramparts.

entities.title: The Skell Archipelago
entities.summary: A jagged chain of granite islets that serve as the stronghold of Torvald's corsair fleet.
entities.content: Surrounded by ship-killing reefs and perpetual sea-fog, the Skell Isles are inaccessible to deep-draft galleys. Torvald's raiders operate slipways and smokehouses along the sheltered inlets of Skell Haven, trading looted grain for southern weapons.

attribution.notes: Boulders on a rocky northern shore bathed in silver moonlight, gazing at distant sails.

entities.title: The Salt Covenant
entities.summary: The oligarchic guild syndicate controlling coastal fisheries, salt pans, and sea trade.
entities.content: A confederation of seven merchant families that hold the Ducal Treasury in suffocating debt. Through their control of the brine-pits, the Covenant dictates the price of preserved winter food. They privately back Lady Lysandra, believing she will protect their commercial privileges against military seizure.

entities.title: The Ashen Liturgy
entities.summary: The ascetic state religion venerating the Sacred Hearth and practicing corpse-salting.
entities.content: The dominant faith across Ostergard. The Liturgy teaches that moisture breeds rot and spiritual decay; the dead must be salted and dried in cliffside bone-houses so their spirits can join the eternal hearth fire. Under Arch-Inquisitor Morwenna, the faith has grown increasingly militant.

attribution.notes: Fiery sepulchers and ascetic inquisitors purging corruption in sacred fire.

entities.title: The Black-Iron Sigil
entities.summary: The ancestral seal ring of House Ostergard, carved from a meteoritic stone dredged from the sea.
entities.content: A massive signet ring carved from a cold, dense star-iron nodule. The seal bears the deep intaglio relief of the sea-eagle and anchor. By sovereign law, any document pressed with blood-wax from this ring possesses absolute legal enforceability across the Bitter Coast.

manuscripts.title: Chapter 2: A Ledger of Cold Embers
manuscripts.content:
The council chamber smelled of wet wool, burning peat, and tallow. At the head of the oak table, where Duke Vane had sat for thirty winters passing death warrants in his thin, spidery hand, Corvus sat with his broadsword laid unbelted before him.

"It is divine castigation," Arch-Inquisitor Morwenna pronounced. She stood by the narrow slit window, her grey cowl casting deep hollows over her cheekbones. Her fingers clicked restlessly along a rosary of charred bone. "The black fungus on the grain stalks is not a sickness of the soil, Lord Warden. It is the rot of heresy. Your father permitted southern pagans to erect their shrine-stones on the headland in exchange for gold ducats. The Sacred Hearth has withdrawn its warmth."

"The Sacred Hearth does not fill a belly, Mother," Lysandra countered from across the table, dipping her quill into black oak-gall ink. "And your monastic tithe-barns in the High Quarter currently hold four hundred tierces of salt-beef that haven't seen the light of day since autumn."

Morwenna's gaze snapped to the Chancellor, pale eyes burning like coals in the hearth. "That beef is consecrated for the holy funeral kilns. Touch it, Lady Vance, and I will have the bells of the Ashen Liturgy toll a curse across your counting-houses before sundown."

Corvus's fist struck the table. The iron blade of Widow's Weight jumped an inch off the oak planks, ringing clear and sharp through the smoke.

The room went deathly still.

"No bells will toll in Dun Carrow without my order," Corvus said, his grey eyes leveling at the Inquisitor. "The tithe-barns will open at noon. Every family with a working hand receives three pounds of meal and a salt herring. The Church may pray over the barrels if it pleases you, Mother. But if a single novice bars the warehouse doors, I will have my border-lances split the timbers with axes."

Morwenna bowed her head, a venomous smile touching the corners of her lips. "The common folk will eat your meal today, my Lord. Let us see what they eat when the snows close the mountain passes in thirty days."

manuscripts.title: Chapter 1: The Salt on the Blade
manuscripts.content:
The sea wind off the Bitter Strait tasted of rust and drowned kelp. It screamed through the embrasures of the High Battery with a sound like dying horses, flinging needles of cold salt-spray against the black basalt ramparts of Dun Carrow.

Lord Corvus Ostergard did not flinch. He leaned his scarred knuckles against the crenellation, watching the grey swell break against the jagged teeth of the Lower Skerries eighty fathoms below. In his nineteen winters along the Northern Wall, he had learned that the cold was not an enemy to be fought, but an auditor that uncovered every flaw in a man's mail and marrow.

"Two more grain-hulks from the Southern Barony ran aground off the Weeping Spit before daybreak, my Lord," a voice said through the wind.

Corvus turned his head slowly. Lady Lysandra Vance stood wrapped in dark lambskin, her silver hair pinned with bone needles against the gale. Under her arm, she clutched the oiled-leather binder that held the daily tally of the realm's slow starvation.

"Were they scuttled?" Corvus asked, his voice harsh from years of shouting over blizzard gales.

"Their rudders were unhung," Lysandra replied smoothly. "Cut clean through with iron saws while they swung at anchor in the roadstead. Torvald's scouts left his branding-chisel hammered into the bowsprit of the lead galley."

Corvus touched the thumb of his left hand. The Black-Iron Sigil was cold against his calloused skin. "Torvald doesn't burn grain. He eats it."

"He didn't burn it, Corvus. He lightered the flour sacks onto three Skell longships before he broached the hulls. Your brother Julian's death bought him the harbor manifests. He knows our granaries have less than six weeks of dry rye remaining before the commons begin boiling harness leather."

Corvus looked past her, toward the lower bailey where three hundred starving dockmen had gathered outside the tithe-gates, their breath rising like smoke into the freezing dawn.

"Then we do not wait for the next convoy," Corvus said, resting his hand on the pommel of Widow's Weight. "Have the harbor chains dropped. Sound the muster at the tide-gate."

Skjaldmær

manuscripts.title: Chapter 3: The Ghost Fleet of Skell
manuscripts.content:
Midnight found Corvus riding through the salt marshes of Mor with six trusted guardsmen, their horses' hooves muffled with oiled burlap. The mist lay thick over the peat pools, smelling of sulphur and decaying reed-beds.

At the mouth of the tidal estuary, where the black shingle met the grey surf, a single iron lantern glowed atop a driftwood spar. Beside it, drawn up on the gravel beach, lay a thirty-oared longship with high, curved dragon-stems.

A tall figure stepped out from the fog, cloaked in wolf-pelts and studded leather. A beard braided with silver wire framed a face mapped with salt-burns and old knife-wounds.

"You've grown thin in the stone cage, little brother," Torvald Black-Thorn said, his deep laughter rumbling over the surf.

"And you've grown bold, Torvald," Corvus said, dismounting into the freezing brine. "Two miles from my coastal battery? If my gunners had spotted your lantern, forty pounds of stone shot would have splintered your oars."

"Your gunners are half-frozen boys from the fens who can't see past their own breath," Torvald spat into the foam. He stepped forward until the two men stood face to face, the cold iron of their swords nearly touching. "I didn't come to burn your hulks, Corvus. I came to tell you who killed Julian."

Corvus's jaw tightened. "My scouts said it was your reavers."

"My reavers use axes and broad-heads," Torvald hissed, leaning in until Corvus could smell the sour ale and salt on his breath. "Julian was poisoned first with nightshade oil, then finished with a southland stiletto. The kind carried by the merchant envoys who sleep in your guest wings."

Torvald reached inside his pelt and pulled out a leather pouch, tossing it at Corvus's chest. It clinked heavily. Corvus unloosed the drawstring. Inside lay twelve gold coins, stamped not with the eagle of Ostergard, but with the crowned sun of the Southern Empire.

"They bought your brother's throat, Corvus," Torvald whispered. "And if you aren't careful, they will buy yours before the spring thaw."
